maturity.evidence: v1.0.20 2026-08-20 is still the latest stable tag, now 73 days old on 2026-11-01 — still the 31-90 day band, so release-recency holds at 1. Only that one release falls inside the trailing 90-day window 2026-08-03 to 2026-11-01, so the in-window count stays at 1 and sustained-cadence holds at 0. major >= 1, so ga-status is unaffected. The repository is not archived, disabled, renamed or transferred (still smtg-ai/claude-squad), but its pushed_at is 2026-08-20, i.e. no commit has landed since the v1.0.20 tag. If no release lands by roughly 2026-11-18 the latest tag crosses 90 days and release-recency falls 1 -> 0, which would lower maturity and the overall score.

No tier-A source found. Re-checked 2026-11-01 and the position is unchanged from the 2026-10-02 check described below, which was re-confirmed page by page: manus.im/updates still holds one undated item, and open.manus.im/docs still carries no changelog, no last-updated stamp, and no dates against API v2 or the deprecated v1. The vendor blog post the updates page links to does carry a byline date, but vendor blog posts are not tier-A evidence under ADR-005, so the verdict stands. The 2026-10-02 finding, unchanged: the gap is narrower but not closed. New this round: open.manus.im/docs is a genuine versioned API reference — an ADR-005 tier-A category — distinguishing API v2 (current) from v1 (deprecated), and it is not labelled Beta. It carries no calendar dates anywhere: no release date for v2, no deprecation date for v1, no last-updated stamps on any page checked. All three Maturity criteria require dates (<= 30 / 31-90 / > 90 days, and a count of stable releases in a trailing 90-day window), and none can be derived from version labels alone. Still 404: manus.im/changelog, manus.im/release-notes, manus.im/help/release-notes, manus.im/docs/api-reference, open.manus.im/docs/changelog. manus.im/updates returns 200 but holds one undated blog link and no dated entries; manus.im/docs/llms.txt indexes the docs and lists no changelog or version-history page; the help-centre root lists eight categories, none of them release notes. The only version-numbered material remains vendor blog copy, which is not evidence under ADR-005.
